plan.title: WT vs KO drug response interaction DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is whether the drug acts differently in knockout than in wild type — an interaction question on a 2x2 factorial (genotype WT/KO x treatment vehicle/drug, 4 replicates per cell, 16 samples, 12,000 genes of human brain bulk RNA-seq counts from Salmon as delivered). Because genotype and treatment each have two levels, the interaction is a single coefficient, so the procedure selects the DESeq2 Wald test on the genotype:treatment interaction (R-0013@2639), with the two simple drug effects (drug effect in WT, drug effect in KO) reported beside it (R-0092@bb58). The counts are a gene-level table from Salmon with no per-sample quantification files and no transcript-length table, so the length-correction state is not established: the model is fitted on the counts as delivered without a length offset, and the report states that isoform-use changes can appear as differential expression (R-0169@18ab, warn). Flow: blind-vst sample-structure QC first (grouping, outliers, library-size pathologies); then one DESeq2 fit with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios size factors, BH within contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, ashr shrinkage of reported fold changes (the KO drug effect is a contrast, not a single coefficient); then fgsea preranked on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome (human subset), and WikiPathways human — run per contrast, primarily on the interaction contrast; and finally a report carrying simple effects and interaction contrast side by side with MA and dispersion diagnostics, p-value histograms, leading-edge genes, and the full reproducibility record. Power note carried into the report: the interaction is a difference of differences with a large standard error, so power is limited at 4 replicates per cell (R-0013@2639). The knowledge check on this plan returned ok with no violations; a planned edgeR quasi-likelihood second-method robustness step was removed because the checked procedure permits only the DESeq2 Wald test for this situation.

steps.name: Interaction report with diagnostics
steps.question: What is the answer to 'does the drug act differently in KO than in WT', with which genes and pathways, at what thresholds, and with what caveats?

plan.title: WT vs KO drug response interaction DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is whether the drug acts differently in knockout than in wild type — an interaction question on a 2x2 factorial (genotype WT/KO x treatment vehicle/drug, 4 replicates per cell, 16 samples, 12,000 genes of human brain bulk RNA-seq counts from Salmon as delivered). Because genotype and treatment each have two levels, the interaction is a single coefficient, so the procedure selects the DESeq2 Wald test on the genotype:treatment interaction (R-0013@2639), with the two simple drug effects (drug effect in WT, drug effect in KO) reported beside it (R-0092@bb58). The counts are a gene-level table from Salmon with no per-sample quantification files and no transcript-length table, so the length-correction state is not established: the model is fitted on the counts as delivered without a length offset, and the report states that isoform-use changes can appear as differential expression (R-0169@18ab, warn). Flow: blind-vst sample-structure QC first (grouping, outliers, library-size pathologies); then one DESeq2 fit with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios size factors, BH within contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, ashr shrinkage of reported fold changes (the KO drug effect is a contrast, not a single coefficient); then fgsea preranked on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome (human subset), and WikiPathways human — run per contrast, primarily on the interaction contrast; and finally a report carrying simple effects and interaction contrast side by side with MA and dispersion diagnostics, p-value histograms, leading-edge genes, and the full reproducibility record. Power note carried into the report: the interaction is a difference of differences with a large standard error, so power is limited at 4 replicates per cell (R-0013@2639). The knowledge check on this plan returned ok with no violations; a planned edgeR quasi-likelihood second-method robustness step was removed because the checked procedure permits only the DESeq2 Wald test for this situation.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
